title: edX Learner and Course Analytics and Visualization Pipeline
author: Michael Ginda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buc3nsyn
materials: Install R statistical software Install R programming language and R Studio Desktop to run the scripts used in this pipeline. Once these pieces of software are installed, you will need to run R Studio. In R studio, you will need to install from the package manager: tcltk2 - a GUI interface used to set paths to access data used in the pipeline. jsonlite - package used for parsing JSON data ndjson - package used for parsing streaming JSON data used in edX event logs. Hmisc - data analytics functions plyr - data aggregation reshape2 - data reshaping functions magrittr - piping functions stringr - string processing and manipulation ggplot2 - statistical visualization package GGally - supplements ggplot2 colorspace - color palette generation R programming language 3.3.3 of later Comprehensive R Archive Network The R Foundation R Studio Desktop 1.1.463 The R Studio, Inc.

steps.title: Review Guide and Secure Data Agreement
steps.instruction: Read the edX Research Guide (https://edx.readthedocs.io/projects/devdata/en/latest/index.html), establish a Data Use Agreement (DUA) and obtain IRB approval before requesting learner data; note that data will be delivered as a ZIP file to be extracted later.

steps.title: Install Gephi and Spatial Ranking
steps.instruction: Install Gephi version 0.8.2 and add the Spatial Ranking layout plugin (https://gephi.org/plugins/#/plugin/spatial-ranking) to enable replication of Figures 1.A and 1.C.

steps.title: Create Project Directory Structure
steps.instruction: Create a workspace that separates original edX course data from processing outputs, e.g. Z:\project\data\edx\{Course_identifier}\ with sub‑folders for course/state data and daily event logs.

steps.title: Extract edX Data Package
steps.instruction: Unzip the provided edX data package into the directory created above, preserving the expected hierarchy (state and events folders) required by the pipeline.

steps.title: Review Processing Scripts
steps.instruction: Examine all R scripts and the UML data‑flow diagram to understand input‑output relationships before execution.

steps.title: Run Course Structure Script
steps.instruction: In RStudio, run edX-1-courseStructureMeta.R, setting correct input and output paths; the script extracts the course hierarchy and automatically creates result directories unless they are removed or commented out.

steps.title: Identify Active Students
steps.instruction: Run edX-2-studentUserList.R to process user‑profile data, exclude instructors, TAs and beta‑testers, and generate a list of active edX user IDs.

steps.title: Extract Individual Event Logs
steps.instruction: Run edX-3-eventLogExtractor.R; it reads daily streaming‑JSON event logs, loops over the active‑student list from the previous step, and writes each student's raw events to a separate CSV file. Processing speed depends on the number of students and their activity volume.

steps.title: Format and Filter Event Logs
steps.instruction: Run edX-4-eventLogFormatter.R to (a) align events to the lowest course‑hierarchy level, (b) add temporal ordering, event‑period calculations and outlier estimates, (c) separate students with fewer than 10 events (these are removed from analysis), and (d) create two new lists of active and inactive students not already excluded. The script uses the course‑structure data from Step 6.

substeps.instruction: Align events to lowest hierarchy level
Compute temporal ordering and period metrics
Generate active and inactive student lists

steps.title: Build Learner Trajectory Networks
steps.instruction: Run edX-5-learnerTrajectoryNet.R; for each student it creates (i) an edge list documenting module‑to‑module transitions and (ii) a node list with interaction statistics for each low‑level module. Export per‑student node and edge CSV files and a combined JSON network file.

steps.title: Aggregate Module Use
steps.instruction: Run edX-6-moduleUseAnalysis.R; it aggregates the node lists from Step 10 using the student ID list from Step 9, producing a course‑wide interaction CSV that can be joined to the course‑structure data from Step 6.

steps.title: Extract Student Features
steps.instruction: Run edX-7-studentFeatureExtraction.R; using metadata from Step 10 and processed logs from Step 9, compute per‑student frequency statistics (sessions, events, unique modules, event types) and temporal usage metrics for overall course and for specific modules/event types.

steps.title: Visualize Course Hierarchy
steps.instruction: In Gephi 0.8.2, load Sample Data A (generated by Script 1) as a node list; duplicate it to create an edge‑list CSV using mod_hex_id as source and parentID as target. Import both files via Data Laboratory and apply the Spatial Ranking layout plugin (nodes positioned along the X‑axis). This reproduces Figure 2.A.

steps.title: Visualize Networks with Spatial Ranking
steps.instruction: Load the JSON or CSV node/edge files produced in Step 10 (e.g., Sample Data Set B) into Gephi’s Data Laboratory, then apply the Spatial Ranking layout (as in Figure 1.C) to generate Figures 2.C and 3. The RMarkdown script for Figure 2.B is at https://cns-iu.github.io/edx-learnertrajectorynetpipeline/edx-8-figure2-B.html and uses Sample Data A and C.

steps.title: Visualize Networks with Force Layout
steps.instruction: Load the same network files into Gephi and apply the Atlas2 force‑directed layout (bundled with Gephi) to produce Figures 2, 4‑6. The RMarkdown scripts are: Figure 3/4 – https://cns-iu.github.io/edx-learnertrajectorynetpipeline/edx-8-figure4and5.html (Sample Data E); Figure 5 – same URL (Sample Data D); Figure 6 – https://cns-iu.github.io/edx-learnertrajectorynetpipeline/edx-8-figure6.html (Sample Data D).

steps.title: Generate Cohort Pathway Networks
steps.instruction: Run edx-8-cohortLearnerPathwaysNet.R, providing (i) a list of student IDs (e.g., enrollment roster, demographic or cluster groups), (ii) the course‑structure data, and (iii) the processed event‑log CSVs. The script builds a group‑level learner transition network with igraph, outputting node statistics (unique student count per module, aggregate interaction counts) and edge statistics (unique student count per path, total traversals). The "dis" measure reports positive values for forward movement and negative values for backward movement based on module order.
